title: Prospective, single-center, randomized, controlled, three-arm pilot study evaluating an eight-week digital diaphragm and respiratory muscle training program in physically active preventive care patients
summary: The diaphragm is the most important breathing muscle. Targeted diaphragmatic breathing leads to deeper and more efficient respiration. This study investigates whether an eight-week digital diaphragm and breathing muscle training program improves respiratory muscle strength and breathing efficiency under physical exertion in physically active adults. Participants are randomly assigned to one of three groups: device-free breathing training, breathing training with a device, or a waitlist control. Respiratory muscle strength, lung performance and other parameters are measured before and after the eight weeks.
conditions: Reduced respiratory muscle strength and breathing economy in physically active adults in a preventive medicine setting

interventions.name: Device-free digital diaphragm and respiratory muscle training (6-phase program, 8 weeks, twice daily, approx. 10–15 minutes per session). Instructional materials provided digitally via videos and PDF training plans.

Waitlist control: no breathing training during the 8-week study period. Participants undergo the same assessment schedule (baseline T0 and follow-up T1). After study completion, the training program is offered to them.

Eight-week classical inspiratory muscle training using a CE-marked breathing training device (e.g. POWERbreathe Medic). Starting load: 50% of individual baseline MIP/PImax. Training volume: 30 breaths per session, twice daily, at least 4 hours apart. Progression independently based on tolerability.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participation in the preventive medical check-up program at the study site. Available baseline diagnostics including MIP/PImax measurement and cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Physically active or regularly exercising person. Ability to perform an eight-week digital respiratory training program. Willingness to attend follow-up assessment after 8 weeks. Access to digital training materials. Written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Known relevant respiratory disease affecting respiratory mechanics (particularly COPD). Relevant unstable cardiovascular disease. Relevant cardiac arrhythmias. History of syncope of unclear cause. Epilepsy. Recent thoracic or abdominal surgery or relevant hernias. Pregnancy. Pronounced panic or hyperventilation tendency if clinically relevant. Acute respiratory infection at time of assessment. Medical contraindication to cardiopulmonary exercise testing or respiratory muscle training. Lack of capacity to consent or lack of consent to data processing. Other medical reasons precluding participation.
